epithet.en: The ageing hidalgo who reads himself into knight-errantry
epithet.da: Den aldrende hidalgo, som læser sig ind i den vandrende ridders verden

1.modern-en: Don Quixote is introduced as an ageing La Mancha hidalgo whose chivalric reading drives him mad and resolves him to become a knight-errant.
1.modern-da: Don Quixote præsenteres som en aldrende hidalgo fra La Mancha, hvis læsning af ridderromaner driver ham til vanvid og får ham til at beslutte sig for at blive vandrende ridder.

2.modern-en: Don Quixote makes his first sally before dawn, arrives at an inn at sunset, and convinces himself it is a castle.
2.modern-da: Don Quixote drager ud på sit første togt før daggry, når frem til en kro ved solnedgang og bilder sig ind, at det er et slot.

3.modern-en: Don Quixote keeps vigil over his armour and persuades the innkeeper to dub him a knight in a mock ceremony.
3.modern-da: Don Quixote holder vagt over sin rustning og overtaler kroværten til at slå ham til ridder ved en latterlig ceremoni.

4.modern-en: Don Quixote rescues the boy Andres from a beating, then attacks merchants who refuse to praise Dulcinea and is left battered.
4.modern-da: Don Quixote redder drengen Andres fra en omgang prygl og angriber derefter nogle købmænd, der nægter at prise Dulcinea, hvorefter han efterlades forslået.

5.modern-en: Don Quixote, beaten and delirious, is found by a neighbour and brought home babbling lines from chivalric romances.
5.modern-da: Don Quixote, slået og forvirret, bliver fundet af en nabo og bragt hjem, mens han plaprer linjer fra ridderromaner.

6.modern-en: Don Quixote sleeps off his bruises while the curate and barber ransack his library and burn most of his books of chivalry.
6.modern-da: Don Quixote sover sine blå mærker væk, mens præsten og barberen rydder hans bibliotek og brænder de fleste af hans ridderromaner.

7.modern-en: Don Quixote, recovered, recruits Sancho Panza as squire on the promise of an island and rides out on his second sally.
7.modern-da: Don Quixote, der nu er kommet sig, hverver Sancho Panza som væbner med løfte om en ø og rider ud på sit andet togt.

8.modern-en: Don Quixote charges the windmills he insists are giants, invoking Dulcinea, and is dashed to the ground with a broken lance.
8.modern-da: Don Quixote stormer mod vejrmøllerne, som han fastholder er kæmper, påkalder Dulcinea og slynges til jorden med en knækket lanse.

9.modern-en: Don Quixote finishes his suspended duel with the Biscayan, splitting his helmet, and spares him at the ladies' request.
9.modern-da: Don Quixote afslutter sin afbrudte tvekamp med biscayeren, kløver hans hjelm og skåner ham på damernes anmodning.

10.modern-en: Don Quixote rides on with Sancho discussing the balm of Fierabras and the laws of knight-errantry while his ear bleeds.
10.modern-da: Don Quixote rider videre med Sancho og taler om Fierabras' balsam og den vandrende ridderskabs love, mens hans øre bløder.

11.modern-en: Don Quixote sups with goatherds and delivers his famous oration on the lost Golden Age beside their fire.
11.modern-da: Don Quixote spiser aftensmad med gedehyrderne og holder sin berømte tale om den tabte gyldne tidsalder ved deres bål.

12.modern-en: Don Quixote listens as a goatherd tells the story of the student-shepherd Chrysostom who has died of love for the shepherdess Marcela.
12.modern-da: Don Quixote lytter, mens en gedehyrde fortæller historien om den studerende hyrde Chrysostom, som er død af kærlighed til hyrdinden Marcela.

13.modern-en: Don Quixote rides to Chrysostom's burial and defends Marcela's right to refuse her suitors before all the mourners.
13.modern-da: Don Quixote rider til Chrysostoms begravelse og forsvarer Marcelas ret til at afvise sine bejlere over for alle de sørgende.

14.modern-en: Don Quixote remains at the funeral as Chrysostom's verses are read, then escorts Marcela away under his protection.
14.modern-da: Don Quixote bliver ved begravelsen, mens Chrysostoms vers læses op, og ledsager derefter Marcela bort under sin beskyttelse.

15.modern-en: Don Quixote is beaten with stakes by Yanguesan carriers after Rocinante tries to mate with their mares.
15.modern-da: Don Quixote bliver slået med stænger af nogle vognmænd fra Yanguas, efter at Rocinante har forsøgt at parre sig med deres hopper.

16.modern-en: Don Quixote, battered, is put to bed at an inn he takes for a castle and is groped in the dark by the servant Maritornes.
16.modern-da: Don Quixote, forslået, lægges til sengs på en kro, han tager for et slot, og bliver i mørket befamlet af tjenestepigen Maritornes.

17.modern-en: Don Quixote brews and drinks the balm of Fierabras, vomits violently, then rides off without paying while Sancho is tossed in a blanket.
17.modern-da: Don Quixote brygger og drikker Fierabras' balsam, kaster voldsomt op og rider derefter af sted uden at betale, mens Sancho kastes op og ned i et tæppe.

18.modern-en: Don Quixote charges two flocks of sheep he insists are the armies of Alifanfaron and Pentapolin, and is stoned by the shepherds.
18.modern-da: Don Quixote stormer mod to fåreflokke, som han insisterer på er hærene under Alifanfaron og Pentapolin, og bliver stenet af hyrderne.

19.modern-en: Don Quixote attacks a procession of mourners carrying a corpse, breaks a bachelor's leg, and dubs himself the Knight of the Rueful Countenance.
19.modern-da: Don Quixote angriber et følge af sørgende, der bærer et lig, brækker benet på en student og udnævner sig selv til Ridderen af den Bedrøvelige Skikkelse.

20.modern-en: Don Quixote, terrified through the night by a pounding noise, discovers at dawn that the dreadful sound came only from fulling-mills.
20.modern-da: Don Quixote, der hele natten har været rædselsslagen over en dunkende lyd, opdager ved daggry, at den frygtelige larm kun kom fra nogle stampemøller.

21.modern-en: Don Quixote takes a barber's brass basin for the helmet of Mambrino, charges the wearer, and rides off with the trophy.
21.modern-da: Don Quixote tager en barbers messingbækken for Mambrinos hjelm, stormer mod manden, der bærer det, og rider af sted med trofæet.

22.modern-en: Don Quixote frees a chain-gang of galley slaves, including Ginés de Pasamonte, and is stoned by them when he demands they visit Dulcinea.
22.modern-da: Don Quixote befrier en lænkebande af galejslaver, deriblandt Ginés de Pasamonte, og bliver stenet af dem, da han forlanger, at de skal opsøge Dulcinea.

23.modern-en: Don Quixote flees with Sancho into the Sierra Morena and finds a portmanteau and notebook belonging to a heartbroken stranger, Cardenio.
23.modern-da: Don Quixote flygter med Sancho ind i Sierra Morena og finder en vadsæk og en notesbog, der tilhører en hjerteknust fremmed ved navn Cardenio.

24.modern-en: Don Quixote meets the half-mad Cardenio in the mountains and listens to the beginning of his tale of betrayal by Don Fernando and Luscinda.
24.modern-da: Don Quixote møder den halvgale Cardenio i bjergene og lytter til begyndelsen af hans fortælling om Don Fernandos og Luscindas forræderi.

25.modern-en: Don Quixote sends Sancho off to Dulcinea with a letter and strips to his shirt to do penance in the Sierra in imitation of Amadis.
25.modern-da: Don Quixote sender Sancho af sted til Dulcinea med et brev og klæder sig af til skjorten for at gøre bod i Sierraen i efterligning af Amadis.

26.modern-en: Don Quixote, alone among the rocks, composes sonnets to Dulcinea and turns somersaults to prove his penitent madness.
26.modern-da: Don Quixote, alene mellem klipperne, digter sonetter til Dulcinea og slår saltomortaler for at bevise sit bodfærdige vanvid.

27.modern-en: Don Quixote is invoked in absentia as the curate and barber set out to lure him home, disguising themselves to play a damsel in distress.
27.modern-da: Don Quixote omtales i sit fravær, mens præsten og barberen drager ud for at lokke ham hjem og forklæder sig for at spille en jomfru i nød.

28.modern-en: Don Quixote remains performing his penance in the Sierra, unseen this chapter, while Dorothea tells her story to the curate and barber.
28.modern-da: Don Quixote bliver ved med at gøre bod i Sierraen og ses ikke i dette kapitel, mens Dorothea fortæller sin historie til præsten og barberen.

29.modern-en: Don Quixote accepts Dorothea, disguised as the Princess Micomicona, as a damsel in distress and agrees to ride out and slay her giant.
29.modern-da: Don Quixote tager imod Dorothea, der er forklædt som prinsesse Micomicona, som en jomfru i nød og indvilliger i at drage ud og dræbe hendes kæmpe.

30.modern-en: Don Quixote listens to Princess Micomicona's invented kingdom-and-giant tale and refuses her offered hand because of his vow to Dulcinea.
30.modern-da: Don Quixote lytter til prinsesse Micomiconas opdigtede fortælling om hendes kongerige og kæmpen og afslår hendes tilbudte hånd på grund af sit løfte til Dulcinea.

31.modern-en: Don Quixote questions Sancho minutely about his fictitious embassy to Dulcinea and then encounters the boy Andres, who curses his earlier rescue.
31.modern-da: Don Quixote udspørger Sancho nøje om hans opdigtede sendefærd til Dulcinea og møder derefter drengen Andres, som forbander hans tidligere redning.

32.modern-en: Don Quixote sleeps at the inn while the curate, the innkeeper, and the others debate the merits of books of chivalry.
32.modern-da: Don Quixote sover på kroen, mens præsten, kroværten og de øvrige diskuterer ridderromanernes værdi.

33.modern-en: Don Quixote sleeps in the garret as the curate reads aloud the novel of "The Ill-Advised Curiosity" to the company at the inn.
33.modern-da: Don Quixote sover på loftskammeret, mens præsten læser fortællingen om "Den ubesindige nysgerrighed" højt for selskabet på kroen.

34.modern-en: Don Quixote remains asleep upstairs while the curate continues reading the novel of Anselmo, Lothario, and Camilla.
34.modern-da: Don Quixote sover stadig ovenpå, mens præsten fortsætter med at læse fortællingen om Anselmo, Lothario og Camilla.

35.modern-en: Don Quixote, sleepwalking through a dream of fighting Micomicona's giant, slashes the innkeeper's wineskins and floods the room with red wine.
35.modern-da: Don Quixote, der i søvne drømmer om at kæmpe mod Micomiconas kæmpe, flænser kroværtens vinsække og oversvømmer rummet med rødvin.

36.modern-en: Don Quixote witnesses but does not interrupt the reunion of Cardenio, Dorothea, Luscinda, and Don Fernando at the inn.
36.modern-da: Don Quixote er vidne til, men afbryder ikke, gensynet mellem Cardenio, Dorothea, Luscinda og Don Fernando på kroen.

37.modern-en: Don Quixote dines with the reunited couples and the newly arrived captive, prefacing the meal with thoughts on Princess Micomicona's quest.
37.modern-da: Don Quixote spiser med de genforenede par og den nyankomne fange og indleder måltidet med betragtninger om prinsesse Micomiconas opgave.

38.modern-en: Don Quixote delivers his great discourse on arms and letters, arguing the soldier's calling above the scholar's.
38.modern-da: Don Quixote holder sin store tale om våben og lærdom, hvori han hævder soldatens kald over for den lærdes.

39.modern-en: Don Quixote listens (or dozes) as the captive recounts his soldiering, his Algerian captivity, and his early years in his father's house.
39.modern-da: Don Quixote lytter (eller døser), mens fangen fortæller om sin soldatertjeneste, sit fangenskab i Algier og sine tidlige år i sin fars hus.

40.modern-en: Don Quixote sits silently among the company while the captive continues his tale of Zoraida and their escape from Algiers.
40.modern-da: Don Quixote sidder tavs blandt selskabet, mens fangen fortsætter sin fortælling om Zoraida og deres flugt fra Algier.

41.modern-en: Don Quixote stays among the listeners as the captive finishes his account of the sea voyage, capture by corsairs, and arrival in Spain.
41.modern-da: Don Quixote bliver blandt tilhørerne, mens fangen afslutter sin beretning om sørejsen, tilfangetagelsen af sørøvere og ankomsten til Spanien.

42.modern-en: Don Quixote retires to sleep while the Judge, the captive's brother, arrives at the inn and reunites with his long-lost sibling.
42.modern-da: Don Quixote trækker sig tilbage for at sove, mens dommeren, fangens bror, ankommer til kroen og genforenes med sin længe savnede slægtning.

43.modern-en: Don Quixote, keeping watch on horseback outside the inn, has his hand tied to a window by Maritornes and is left hanging till dawn.
43.modern-da: Don Quixote, der holder vagt til hest uden for kroen, får sin hånd bundet til et vindue af Maritornes og efterlades hængende til daggry.

44.modern-en: Don Quixote refuses to fight the officers seeking him and presides over the quarrels between Dorothea, the muleteer, and the innkeeper.
44.modern-da: Don Quixote nægter at kæmpe mod betjentene, der søger ham, og afgør stridighederne mellem Dorothea, muldyrdriveren og kroværten.

45.modern-en: Don Quixote rules definitively that the barber's basin is Mambrino's helmet, then routs an officer of the Holy Brotherhood who tries to arrest him.
45.modern-da: Don Quixote afgør endegyldigt, at barberens bækken er Mambrinos hjelm, og slår derefter en betjent fra Det Hellige Broderskab på flugt, da denne forsøger at anholde ham.

46.modern-en: Don Quixote accepts the curate's ruse, allows himself to be bound and caged on an ox-cart, believing he is under enchantment.
46.modern-da: Don Quixote tror på præstens list, lader sig binde og spærre inde i et bur på en oksekærre i den tro, at han er forhekset.

47.modern-en: Don Quixote, caged on the ox-cart, debates the enchantment with Sancho and listens to a canon they meet on the road denounce books of chivalry.
47.modern-da: Don Quixote, indespærret i buret på oksekærren, diskuterer forheksningen med Sancho og lytter til en kannik, de møder på vejen, fordømme ridderromanerne.

48.modern-en: Don Quixote argues with the canon from inside his cage, defending the truth of chivalric histories against the canon's literary critique.
48.modern-da: Don Quixote skændes med kanniken inde fra sit bur og forsvarer ridderhistoriernes sandhed mod kannikens litterære kritik.

49.modern-en: Don Quixote, released from the cage to eat, debates Sancho about his enchantment and rehearses heroes of romance as historical fact.
49.modern-da: Don Quixote, der slippes ud af buret for at spise, diskuterer sin forheksning med Sancho og opremser helte fra romanerne som historiske kendsgerninger.

50.modern-en: Don Quixote answers the canon with an exuberant account of the Knight of the Lake to prove the delight chivalric reading offers.
50.modern-da: Don Quixote svarer kanniken med en overstrømmende fortælling om Ridderen ved Søen for at bevise den glæde, læsning af ridderromaner giver.

51.modern-en: Don Quixote eats with the goatherd Eugenio and listens to his pastoral tale of the runaway Leandra and her seducer Vicente.
51.modern-da: Don Quixote spiser med gedehyrden Eugenio og lytter til hans pastorale fortælling om den bortløbne Leandra og hendes forfører Vicente.

52.modern-en: Don Quixote fights the goatherd, then charges a procession of penitents carrying an image of the Virgin and is finally carted home to his village.
52.modern-da: Don Quixote slås med gedehyrden, stormer derefter mod et følge af bodgørere, der bærer et billede af Jomfruen, og bliver til sidst kørt hjem til sin landsby.

53.modern-en: Don Quixote is visited at home by the curate and barber, who probe his sanity until he reveals his mind is still set on chivalry.
53.modern-da: Don Quixote får besøg i sit hjem af præsten og barberen, der udforsker hans forstand, indtil han afslører, at hans sind stadig er optaget af ridderskabet.

54.modern-en: Don Quixote receives the bachelor Samson Carrasco and learns that the first part of his own history has been printed and read all over Spain.
54.modern-da: Don Quixote tager imod studenten Samson Carrasco og erfarer, at første del af hans egen historie er blevet trykt og læst over hele Spanien.

55.modern-en: Don Quixote interrogates Samson Carrasco about the published book of his exploits and resolves to set out on a third sally.
55.modern-da: Don Quixote udspørger Samson Carrasco om den udgivne bog om hans bedrifter og beslutter sig for at drage ud på et tredje togt.

56.modern-en: Don Quixote stays out of the kitchen quarrels while Sancho fences with Carrasco over the printed history's mistakes.
56.modern-da: Don Quixote holder sig ude af køkkenskænderierne, mens Sancho diskuterer med Carrasco om fejlene i den trykte historie.

57.modern-en: Don Quixote prepares secretly for the third sally while Sancho, at home, argues with Teresa about taking up squireship again.
57.modern-da: Don Quixote forbereder sig i hemmelighed på det tredje togt, mens Sancho derhjemme skændes med Teresa om at påtage sig væbnertjenesten igen.

58.modern-en: Don Quixote endures his niece's and housekeeper's pleas not to leave, defending knight-errantry with a lecture on lineage and virtue.
58.modern-da: Don Quixote udholder sin nieces og husholderskes bønner om ikke at rejse og forsvarer den vandrende ridderskab med en belæring om byrd og dyd.

59.modern-en: Don Quixote sets out at last for El Toboso with Sancho, planning to seek Dulcinea's blessing before any new adventure.
59.modern-da: Don Quixote drager omsider af sted mod El Toboso med Sancho og agter at søge Dulcineas velsignelse før noget nyt eventyr.

60.modern-en: Don Quixote rides toward El Toboso debating fame, sanctity, and chivalry with Sancho on the road.
60.modern-da: Don Quixote rider mod El Toboso, mens han på vejen diskuterer berømmelse, hellighed og ridderskab med Sancho.

61.modern-en: Don Quixote enters El Toboso at midnight, finds no palace of Dulcinea, and sends Sancho into the village to locate her.
61.modern-da: Don Quixote rider ind i El Toboso ved midnat, finder intet palads tilhørende Dulcinea og sender Sancho ind i landsbyen for at finde hende.

62.modern-en: Don Quixote accepts as Dulcinea the coarse village girl Sancho points out and concludes that enchanters have transformed her.
62.modern-da: Don Quixote accepterer den grove landsbypige, som Sancho udpeger, som Dulcinea og slutter, at troldmænd har forvandlet hende.

63.modern-en: Don Quixote meets the cart of strolling players costumed as Death, Cupid, and the Devil, and lets the company pass without a fight.
63.modern-da: Don Quixote møder en kærre med omrejsende skuespillere udklædt som Døden, Amor og Djævelen og lader selskabet passere uden kamp.

64.modern-en: Don Quixote camps in a wood and meets the Knight of the Mirrors, who claims to have already defeated him in battle.
64.modern-da: Don Quixote slår lejr i en skov og møder Spejlenes Ridder, der hævder allerede at have besejret ham i kamp.

65.modern-en: Don Quixote sleeps under the trees while Sancho and the squire of the Mirrors debate squireship and wages.
65.modern-da: Don Quixote sover under træerne, mens Sancho og Spejlenes Ridders væbner diskuterer væbnertjeneste og løn.

66.modern-en: Don Quixote unhorses the Knight of the Mirrors at dawn and discovers his face is that of Samson Carrasco.
66.modern-da: Don Quixote slår Spejlenes Ridder af hesten ved daggry og opdager, at hans ansigt er Samson Carrascos.

67.modern-en: Don Quixote rides off triumphant, never doubting that enchanters gave Samson Carrasco's face to his beaten rival.
67.modern-da: Don Quixote rider triumferende videre uden et øjeblik at tvivle på, at troldmænd har givet Samson Carrascos ansigt til hans besejrede modstander.

68.modern-en: Don Quixote falls in with Don Diego de Miranda, the Knight of the Green Coat, and discourses with him on knight-errantry.
68.modern-da: Don Quixote slår følge med Don Diego de Miranda, Ridderen i den Grønne Kappe, og samtaler med ham om den vandrende ridderskab.

69.modern-en: Don Quixote insists a cart carrying caged lions be opened and confronts the great male lion, who only yawns and lies down.
69.modern-da: Don Quixote forlanger, at en kærre med løver i bur skal åbnes, og stiller sig over for den store hanløve, der blot gaber og lægger sig ned.

70.modern-en: Don Quixote stays at Don Diego de Miranda's house, meets his poet son Lorenzo, and judges his verses with surprising sanity.
70.modern-da: Don Quixote bor hos Don Diego de Miranda, møder dennes digtersøn Lorenzo og bedømmer hans vers med overraskende klarsyn.

71.modern-en: Don Quixote rides on and falls in with students bound for the wedding of Camacho the rich and the beautiful Quiteria.
71.modern-da: Don Quixote rider videre og slår følge med nogle studerende, der er på vej til brylluppet mellem den rige Camacho og den smukke Quiteria.

72.modern-en: Don Quixote attends Camacho's lavish wedding feast and watches the poor Basilio stage a feigned suicide to win Quiteria.
72.modern-da: Don Quixote deltager i Camachos overdådige bryllupsfest og ser den fattige Basilio iscenesætte et foregivet selvmord for at vinde Quiteria.

73.modern-en: Don Quixote defends Basilio's stratagem sword in hand and rides off with the new couple toward Basilio's village.
73.modern-da: Don Quixote forsvarer Basilios list med sværd i hånd og rider af sted med det nye par mod Basilios landsby.

74.modern-en: Don Quixote is lowered by rope into the deep cave of Montesinos to investigate its marvels.
74.modern-da: Don Quixote sænkes ned i den dybe Montesinos-hule i et reb for at undersøge dens undere.

75.modern-en: Don Quixote, hauled back up, recounts a vision of Montesinos, Durandarte's heart, and an enchanted Dulcinea begging for a loan of six reales.
75.modern-da: Don Quixote, der er hejst op igen, fortæller om et syn af Montesinos, Durandartes hjerte og en forhekset Dulcinea, der tigger om et lån på seks reales.

76.modern-en: Don Quixote rides on with Sancho and the cousin, lodges at an inn, and hears of the braying villages and Master Pedro the puppeteer.
76.modern-da: Don Quixote rider videre med Sancho og fætteren, tager ind på en kro og hører om de gøende landsbyer og dukkeføreren Mester Pedro.

77.modern-en: Don Quixote watches Master Pedro's divining ape, then Master Pedro's puppet show of Melisendra's rescue by Don Gaiferos.
77.modern-da: Don Quixote ser Mester Pedros spående abe og derefter Mester Pedros dukketeater om Don Gaiferos' redning af Melisendra.

78.modern-en: Don Quixote, swept up by the puppet-show, draws his sword and slashes the Moorish puppets to pieces, then pays for the damage.
78.modern-da: Don Quixote, revet med af dukketeatret, trækker sit sværd og hugger de mauriske dukker i stykker og betaler derefter for skaden.

79.modern-en: Don Quixote meets the braying villages drawn up for battle and is left behind as Sancho is beaten and unhorsed.
79.modern-da: Don Quixote møder de gøende landsbyer opstillet til kamp og efterlades, mens Sancho bliver slået og kastet af hesten.

80.modern-en: Don Quixote and Sancho ride away from the braying villagers and reach the banks of the river Ebro.
80.modern-da: Don Quixote og Sancho rider bort fra de gøende landsbyboere og når frem til bredden af floden Ebro.

81.modern-en: Don Quixote steps aboard an empty boat on the Ebro, certain it is enchanted, and is overturned and dragged from the water by fishermen's nets.
81.modern-da: Don Quixote går om bord i en tom båd på Ebro, overbevist om at den er forhekset, og bliver væltet og trukket op af vandet i fiskernes net.

82.modern-en: Don Quixote meets a duchess hunting with falcons in a wood and accepts her invitation to her nearby castle.
82.modern-da: Don Quixote møder en hertuginde, der jager med falke i en skov, og tager imod hendes invitation til hendes nærliggende slot.

83.modern-en: Don Quixote is welcomed into the duke and duchess's castle as a true knight-errant and dines under elaborate ceremony.
83.modern-da: Don Quixote bydes velkommen på hertugens og hertugindens slot som en ægte vandrende ridder og spiser under omstændelig ceremoni.

84.modern-en: Don Quixote answers an ecclesiastic who scolds him for his mad chivalry, then advises Sancho as the duke confirms the governorship.
84.modern-da: Don Quixote svarer en gejstlig, der skænder på ham for hans gale ridderskab, og rådgiver derefter Sancho, mens hertugen bekræfter statholderskabet.

85.modern-en: Don Quixote sits dining while the duchess teases Sancho into pronouncing on Dulcinea's reality and his own qualifications to govern.
85.modern-da: Don Quixote sidder til bords, mens hertuginden driller Sancho til at udtale sig om Dulcineas virkelighed og sine egne evner til at regere.

86.modern-en: Don Quixote takes part in a staged forest pageant where Merlin announces that Dulcinea can only be disenchanted by Sancho's three thousand lashes.
86.modern-da: Don Quixote deltager i et iscenesat skovoptrin, hvor Merlin forkynder, at Dulcinea kun kan løses fra forheksningen ved Sanchos tre tusind piskeslag.

87.modern-en: Don Quixote pleads with Sancho to accept the penance, while the duchess and duke continue their theatrical game.
87.modern-da: Don Quixote bønfalder Sancho om at tage imod boden, mens hertuginden og hertugen fortsætter deres teaterspil.

88.modern-en: Don Quixote receives the Distressed Duenna, the bearded Countess Trifaldi, and pledges himself to undo her enchantment.
88.modern-da: Don Quixote tager imod den Bedrøvede Hofdame, den skæggede grevinde Trifaldi, og lover at ophæve hendes forheksning.

89.modern-en: Don Quixote listens as the Countess Trifaldi tells the long tale of Princess Antonomasia and the giant Malambruno.
89.modern-da: Don Quixote lytter, mens grevinde Trifaldi fortæller den lange historie om prinsesse Antonomasia og kæmpen Malambruno.

90.modern-en: Don Quixote listens as the Trifaldi finishes her story and the bearded duennas weep over their punishment.
90.modern-da: Don Quixote lytter, mens Trifaldi afslutter sin historie, og de skæggede hofdamer græder over deres straf.

91.modern-en: Don Quixote pledges to ride the wooden horse Clavileño and break Malambruno's spell.
91.modern-da: Don Quixote lover at ride træhesten Clavileño og bryde Malambrunos fortryllelse.

92.modern-en: Don Quixote and Sancho are blindfolded onto Clavileño, are pretended-flown through the sky, and find themselves back in the garden after a firework explosion.
92.modern-da: Don Quixote og Sancho bindes for øjnene og sættes op på Clavileño, foregives at flyve gennem himlen og finder sig selv tilbage i haven efter en fyrværkerieksplosion.

93.modern-en: Don Quixote pretends to corroborate Sancho's fantastic account of what they saw aloft on Clavileño.
93.modern-da: Don Quixote foregiver at bekræfte Sanchos fantastiske beretning om, hvad de så højt oppe på Clavileño.

94.modern-en: Don Quixote takes Sancho aside and gives him a long, serious course of advice on how to govern his island justly and humbly.
94.modern-da: Don Quixote tager Sancho til side og giver ham et langt, alvorligt forløb af råd om, hvordan han skal regere sin ø retfærdigt og ydmygt.

95.modern-en: Don Quixote gives Sancho a second set of counsels, this time on personal manners, dress, table behaviour, and rhetoric.
95.modern-da: Don Quixote giver Sancho endnu et sæt råd, denne gang om personlige manerer, påklædning, bordskik og veltalenhed.

96.modern-en: Don Quixote, alone in his room after Sancho's departure, is mauled in the dark by a basket of cats let in through the window.
96.modern-da: Don Quixote, alene i sit værelse efter Sanchos afrejse, bliver i mørket forrevet af en kurv katte, der lukkes ind gennem vinduet.

97.modern-en: Don Quixote is absent while Sancho takes possession of his island of Barataria and judges his first cases.
97.modern-da: Don Quixote er fraværende, mens Sancho tager sin ø Barataria i besiddelse og dømmer i sine første sager.

98.modern-en: Don Quixote, recovering from the cats, is serenaded outside his window by the duchess's maid Altisidora pretending to be in love with him.
98.modern-da: Don Quixote, der kommer sig efter kattene, får udenfor sit vindue en serenade af hertugindens kammerpige Altisidora, der foregiver at være forelsket i ham.

99.modern-en: Don Quixote remains at the castle while Sancho governs Barataria, hears more cases, and is hurried off by the duke's steward.
99.modern-da: Don Quixote bliver på slottet, mens Sancho regerer Barataria, hører flere sager og skyndes af sted af hertugens hovmester.

100.modern-en: Don Quixote receives a midnight visit from Doña Rodriguez and listens to her tale of her daughter's seduction by a young farmer.
100.modern-da: Don Quixote får et midnatsbesøg af Doña Rodriguez og lytter til hendes fortælling om sin datters forførelse af en ung bonde.

101.modern-en: Don Quixote, absent from this chapter, while Sancho patrols Barataria at night and gives judgement on the various rogues he catches.
101.modern-da: Don Quixote er fraværende i dette kapitel, mens Sancho patruljerer Barataria om natten og dømmer de forskellige slyngler, han fanger.

102.modern-en: Don Quixote is invoked from afar as the duke's people reveal the enchanters behind Altisidora's tricks and the page delivers Sancho's letter to Teresa.
102.modern-da: Don Quixote omtales på afstand, mens hertugens folk afslører troldmændene bag Altisidoras narrestreger, og pagen overbringer Sanchos brev til Teresa.

103.modern-en: Don Quixote remains at the castle while Sancho governs Barataria with growing weariness.
103.modern-da: Don Quixote bliver på slottet, mens Sancho regerer Barataria med voksende træthed.

104.modern-en: Don Quixote sits in the castle while Doña Rodriguez brings her dishonoured daughter and demands a champion against the farmer who deceived her.
104.modern-da: Don Quixote sidder på slottet, mens Doña Rodriguez bringer sin vanærede datter og kræver en forkæmper mod bonden, der har bedraget hende.

105.modern-en: Don Quixote is absent as Sancho, after the staged invasion of Barataria, lays down his governorship and rides back toward his master.
105.modern-da: Don Quixote er fraværende, da Sancho efter den iscenesatte invasion af Barataria nedlægger sit statholderskab og rider tilbage mod sin herre.

106.modern-en: Don Quixote, mourning his lonely state at the castle, prepares to meet the lacquey Tosilos in the lists on Doña Rodriguez's daughter's behalf.
106.modern-da: Don Quixote, der sørger over sin ensomme tilstand på slottet, forbereder sig på at møde lakajen Tosilos i skranken på Doña Rodriguez' datters vegne.

107.modern-en: Don Quixote is referred to from afar as Sancho, on the road back to the castle, meets his old neighbour Ricote the Morisco.
107.modern-da: Don Quixote omtales på afstand, mens Sancho på vej tilbage til slottet møder sin gamle nabo Ricote, morisken.

108.modern-en: Don Quixote takes the lists against Tosilos, who refuses to fight and declares he will marry Doña Rodriguez's daughter on the spot.
108.modern-da: Don Quixote går ind i skranken mod Tosilos, der nægter at kæmpe og erklærer, at han på stedet vil gifte sig med Doña Rodriguez' datter.

109.modern-en: Don Quixote takes leave of the duke and duchess and rides off with Sancho, refusing further hospitality despite Altisidora's mock laments.
109.modern-da: Don Quixote tager afsked med hertugen og hertuginden og rider bort med Sancho, idet han afslår yderligere gæstfrihed trods Altisidoras spottende klager.

110.modern-en: Don Quixote falls in with peasants carrying images of saints, takes them as fellow knights-errant of God, and rides on with Sancho.
110.modern-da: Don Quixote slår følge med bønder, der bærer helgenbilleder, tager dem for vandrende Guds riddere og rider videre med Sancho.

111.modern-en: Don Quixote and Sancho lodge at an inn that is not a castle and meet two gentlemen reading the spurious Avellaneda sequel.
111.modern-da: Don Quixote og Sancho tager ind på en kro, der ikke er et slot, og møder to herrer, der læser den uægte fortsættelse af Avellaneda.

112.modern-en: Don Quixote, indignant at the false sequel, resolves to go to Barcelona rather than Saragossa to give the lie to Avellaneda's book.
112.modern-da: Don Quixote, forarget over den falske fortsættelse, beslutter sig for at tage til Barcelona i stedet for Zaragoza for at gøre Avellanedas bog til løgn.

113.modern-en: Don Quixote enters Barcelona at dawn, is welcomed by Don Antonio Moreno, and rides through the city as the famous knight-errant of the printed history.
113.modern-da: Don Quixote rider ind i Barcelona ved daggry, bydes velkommen af Don Antonio Moreno og rider gennem byen som den berømte vandrende ridder fra den trykte historie.

114.modern-en: Don Quixote consults Don Antonio's "enchanted head," which answers his questions about Dulcinea and his own future with cryptic phrases.
114.modern-da: Don Quixote rådspørger Don Antonios "forheksede hoved", som besvarer hans spørgsmål om Dulcinea og hans egen fremtid med kryptiske ord.

115.modern-en: Don Quixote watches the Barcelona galleys with Sancho and witnesses the Morisco girl Ana Felix tell her tale to the viceroy.
115.modern-da: Don Quixote ser på Barcelonas galejer sammen med Sancho og er vidne til, at den moriske pige Ana Felix fortæller sin historie til vicekongen.

116.modern-en: Don Quixote is unhorsed on the Barcelona beach by the Knight of the White Moon and swears to lay down arms for a year.
116.modern-da: Don Quixote kastes af hesten på stranden ved Barcelona af Ridderen af den Hvide Måne og sværger at nedlægge våbnene i et år.

117.modern-en: Don Quixote stays bedridden six days in Barcelona digesting his defeat by the Knight of the White Moon, who is again revealed as Samson Carrasco.
117.modern-da: Don Quixote ligger sengeliggende i seks dage i Barcelona, mens han fordøjer sit nederlag til Ridderen af den Hvide Måne, der atter viser sig at være Samson Carrasco.

118.modern-en: Don Quixote, on the road home, meets Tosilos again and learns the duke had forced him to fight in the lacquey's place after all.
118.modern-da: Don Quixote møder på vej hjem atter Tosilos og erfarer, at hertugen alligevel havde tvunget ham til at kæmpe i lakajens sted.

119.modern-en: Don Quixote resolves to spend his year of penance as a shepherd named Quixotiz in pastoral retirement with Sancho.
119.modern-da: Don Quixote beslutter at tilbringe sit boddsår som hyrde ved navn Quixotiz i pastoral afsondring med Sancho.

120.modern-en: Don Quixote is trampled by a herd of pigs as he and Sancho lie sleeping at the roadside.
120.modern-da: Don Quixote bliver trampet ned af en flok svin, mens han og Sancho ligger og sover ved vejkanten.

121.modern-en: Don Quixote, back at the duke's castle, finds Altisidora staged on a bier and Sancho pinched to bring her back to life.
121.modern-da: Don Quixote, tilbage på hertugens slot, finder Altisidora iscenesat på en båre og Sancho knebet for at bringe hende tilbage til livet.

122.modern-en: Don Quixote endures Altisidora's mock-amorous reproaches at the castle and finally takes leave once more.
122.modern-da: Don Quixote udholder Altisidoras spottende kærlighedsbebrejdelser på slottet og tager til sidst afsked endnu en gang.

123.modern-en: Don Quixote and Sancho ride homeward debating the pastoral life and the lashes still owed to disenchant Dulcinea.
123.modern-da: Don Quixote og Sancho rider hjemad, mens de diskuterer hyrdelivet og de piskeslag, der endnu skyldes for at løse Dulcinea fra forheksningen.

124.modern-en: Don Quixote and Sancho reach their village and meet Samson Carrasco and the curate at its outskirts.
124.modern-da: Don Quixote og Sancho når deres landsby og møder Samson Carrasco og præsten i udkanten.

125.modern-en: Don Quixote enters his village reading ill omens into a hare's flight and a boys' quarrel, fearing he will never see Dulcinea again.
125.modern-da: Don Quixote rider ind i sin landsby og tolker onde varsler i en hares flugt og et drengeskænderi, idet han frygter, at han aldrig vil se Dulcinea igen.

126.modern-en: Don Quixote falls ill in bed, recovers his sanity, renounces chivalry as Alonso Quixano the Good, makes his will, and dies a Christian death.
126.modern-da: Don Quixote bliver syg og sengeliggende, genvinder sin forstand, forsager ridderskabet som Alonso Quixano den Gode, opretter sit testamente og dør en kristen død.

epithet.en: The peasant squire who follows Don Quixote for the promise of an island
epithet.da: Den bondesquire, der følger Don Quixote for løftet om en ø at regere

7.modern-en: Sancho Panza is recruited as squire on the promise of an island, mounts his donkey, and rides out with Don Quixote on the second sally.
7.modern-da: Sancho Panza bliver hvervet som væbner mod løftet om en ø, sætter sig op på sit æsel og rider ud med Don Quixote på det andet togt.

8.modern-en: Sancho watches in horror as Don Quixote charges the windmills, then patches him up and begs him to remember that not every shape is what it seems.
8.modern-da: Sancho ser med rædsel på, mens Don Quixote angriber vindmøllerne, lapper ham derefter sammen og bønfalder ham om at huske, at ikke enhver skikkelse er, hvad den ser ud til at være.

9.modern-en: Sancho is described in the Arabic manuscript that Cide Hamete Benengeli is supposed to have authored, long-legged and pot-bellied beside Rocinante.
9.modern-da: Sancho beskrives i det arabiske manuskript, som Cide Hamete Benengeli efter sigende skal have forfattet, langbenet og tykmavet ved siden af Rocinante.

10.modern-en: Sancho dresses his master's wounds, hears about the holy balm of Fierabras, and starts to suspect his island will cost him dear.
10.modern-da: Sancho forbinder sin herres sår, hører om Fierabras' hellige balsam og begynder at fornemme, at hans ø vil komme til at koste ham dyrt.

11.modern-en: Sancho eats with the goatherds while Don Quixote orates about the Golden Age, more interested in the wineskin than the speech.
11.modern-da: Sancho spiser sammen med gedehyrderne, mens Don Quixote holder tale om Guldalderen, mere optaget af vinsækken end af talen.

12.modern-en: Sancho listens with the goatherds to the tale of Marcela and Chrysostom, mostly waiting for the food to come round again.
12.modern-da: Sancho lytter sammen med gedehyrderne til fortællingen om Marcela og Chrysostomos, mest mens han venter på, at maden skal komme rundt igen.

13.modern-en: Sancho rides with the company to the shepherd's burial and watches Marcela defend herself before the mourners.
13.modern-da: Sancho rider med følget til hyrdens begravelse og ser Marcela forsvare sig over for de sørgende.

15.modern-en: Sancho is cudgelled along with his master by the Yangüesan carriers after Rocinante's lust for their mares provokes the brawl.
15.modern-da: Sancho bliver prygløs sammen med sin herre af de yanguesiske drivere, efter at Rocinantes lyst til deres hopper har udløst slagsmålet.

16.modern-en: Sancho is half-killed in the dark loft of the inn when Maritornes's mistaken visit ends in a brawl among him, the carrier, the innkeeper, and the officer.
16.modern-da: Sancho bliver halvt slået ihjel i kroens mørke loftskammer, da Maritornes' fejltagne besøg ender i et slagsmål mellem ham, driveren, kroværten og betjenten.

17.modern-en: Sancho drinks the holy balm of Fierabras and is violently sick at both ends, then is tossed in a blanket by mischievous guests as Don Quixote rides away.
17.modern-da: Sancho drikker Fierabras' hellige balsam og bliver voldsomt dårlig i begge ender, hvorefter han bliver kastet op i et lagen af kådefulde gæster, mens Don Quixote rider bort.

18.modern-en: Sancho watches Don Quixote charge a flock of sheep he insists is an army, and helps him spit teeth back into place when the shepherds stone him.
18.modern-da: Sancho ser Don Quixote angribe en fåreflok, som han hævder er en hær, og hjælper ham med at spytte tænderne på plads igen, da hyrderne stener ham.

19.modern-en: Sancho rechristens his master "the Knight of the Sorrowful Countenance" after the night encounter with the corpse-bearers.
19.modern-da: Sancho omdøber sin herre til »Ridderen af den Bedrøvelige Skikkelse« efter natmødet med ligbærerne.

20.modern-en: Sancho ties Rocinante's legs together so they cannot ride toward the dreadful pounding in the dark, tells a winding rustic tale to keep his master awake, and finally relieves himself in his master's presence to fill the night.
20.modern-da: Sancho binder Rocinantes ben sammen, så de ikke kan ride mod den frygtelige dunken i mørket, fortæller en snørklet bondefortælling for at holde sin herre vågen og forretter til sidst sin nødtørft i sin herres nærvær for at få natten til at gå.

21.modern-en: Sancho gleefully claims the muleteer's pack-saddle and trappings after Don Quixote takes the barber's basin as Mambrino's helmet.
21.modern-da: Sancho tilegner sig fornøjet muldyrdriverens pakkesaddel og seletøj, efter at Don Quixote har taget barberens fad som Mambrinos hjelm.

22.modern-en: Sancho is robbed and stoned along with his master by the galley slaves Don Quixote has just set free.
22.modern-da: Sancho bliver bestjålet og stenet sammen med sin herre af de galejslaver, Don Quixote netop har sat fri.

23.modern-en: Sancho loses his donkey to the thief Ginés de Pasamonte in the Sierra Morena and weeps openly for the missing beast.
23.modern-da: Sancho mister sit æsel til tyven Ginés de Pasamonte i Sierra Morena og græder åbenlyst over det forsvundne dyr.

24.modern-en: Sancho listens with Don Quixote to the Ragged Knight Cardenio's tale of love and betrayal in the wilderness.
24.modern-da: Sancho lytter sammen med Don Quixote til den pjaltede ridder Cardenios fortælling om kærlighed og forræderi i vildmarken.

25.modern-en: Sancho is sent to El Toboso with a letter to Dulcinea while Don Quixote strips half-naked to do penance among the rocks in imitation of Amadis.
25.modern-da: Sancho bliver sendt til El Toboso med et brev til Dulcinea, mens Don Quixote klæder sig halvnøgen og gør bod blandt klipperne i efterligning af Amadís.

26.modern-en: Sancho rides out of the Sierra rehearsing the letter, then runs into the curate and the barber and is talked out of going to El Toboso at all.
26.modern-da: Sancho rider ud af Sierraen, mens han øver brevet udenad, støder så på præsten og barberen og bliver talt fra overhovedet at tage til El Toboso.

27.modern-en: Sancho is enlisted by the curate and barber in their plan to bring Don Quixote home, his loyalty to his master mixed with his hunger for the island.
27.modern-da: Sancho bliver hvervet af præsten og barberen til deres plan om at bringe Don Quixote hjem, hans troskab mod sin herre blandet med hans grådighed efter øen.

29.modern-en: Sancho greets the disguised "Princess Micomicona" with delight, already calculating the worth of his island in a kingdom so rich.
29.modern-da: Sancho hilser den forklædte »prinsesse Micomicona« med glæde, allerede i færd med at beregne værdien af sin ø i et så rigt kongerige.

30.modern-en: Sancho is dismayed when the imagined kingdom of Micomicona threatens the very Dulcinea he is supposed to deliver letters to, and asks how an island will come of it.
30.modern-da: Sancho bliver bestyrtet, da det forestillede kongerige Micomicona truer netop den Dulcinea, han skal bringe breve til, og spørger, hvordan der dog skal komme en ø ud af det.

31.modern-en: Sancho describes a wholly invented visit to Dulcinea, painting her winnowing wheat and dispatching him back to her knight with hearty country greetings.
31.modern-da: Sancho beskriver et fuldstændig opdigtet besøg hos Dulcinea og maler hende, mens hun renser hvede og sender ham tilbage til sin ridder med hjertelige landlige hilsener.

32.modern-en: Sancho defends his master and his romances at the inn against the curate's gentler scepticism.
32.modern-da: Sancho forsvarer sin herre og hans ridderromaner på kroen mod præstens mildere skepsis.

35.modern-en: Sancho watches in awe as Don Quixote slashes the wineskins to ribbons in his sleep, convinced his master has slain the giant of Micomicona.
35.modern-da: Sancho ser med ærefrygt på, mens Don Quixote i søvne flænser vinsækkene i laser, overbevist om at hans herre har dræbt Micomiconas kæmpe.

36.modern-en: Sancho is present as the reunited lovers (Dorotea, Don Fernando, Cardenio, Luscinda) sort themselves out at the inn.
36.modern-da: Sancho er til stede, mens de genforenede elskende (Dorotea, Don Fernando, Cardenio, Luscinda) finder ud af deres forviklinger på kroen.

37.modern-en: Sancho is troubled to see Micomicona shrink back into Dorotea, and worries aloud about what becomes of his island now.
37.modern-da: Sancho bliver foruroliget over at se Micomicona forvandle sig tilbage til Dorotea og bekymrer sig højlydt om, hvad der nu bliver af hans ø.

38.modern-en: Sancho listens to Don Quixote's speech comparing arms and letters at the inn table.
38.modern-da: Sancho lytter til Don Quixotes tale, der sammenligner våben og lærdom, ved kroens bord.

42.modern-en: Sancho is present at the inn as the captive's tale gives way to the arrival of the judge.
42.modern-da: Sancho er til stede på kroen, da fangens fortælling afløses af dommerens ankomst.

43.modern-en: Sancho is helpless beneath the window as his master hangs suspended by the wrist from Maritornes's strap, his bare feet barely brushing Rocinante's back.
43.modern-da: Sancho står hjælpeløst under vinduet, mens hans herre hænger og dingler fra håndleddet i Maritornes' rem, med sine bare fødder lige akkurat strejfende Rocinantes ryg.

44.modern-en: Sancho insists on his island and his master's identity even as the company at the inn quietly arranges for the cage that will take Don Quixote home.
44.modern-da: Sancho fastholder kravet på sin ø og sin herres identitet, selv mens følget på kroen i al stilhed sørger for det bur, der skal bringe Don Quixote hjem.

45.modern-en: Sancho swears that the basin is Mambrino's helmet and the pack-saddle a caparison, dragging the whole inn into his master's delusion.
45.modern-da: Sancho sværger på, at fadet er Mambrinos hjelm og pakkesaddelen et hesteklæde, og trækker hele kroen ind i sin herres vildfarelse.

46.modern-en: Sancho is bewildered when masked figures cage Don Quixote in an ox-cart and explain that his master has been enchanted by sages.
46.modern-da: Sancho bliver forbløffet, da maskerede skikkelser spærrer Don Quixote inde i en oksekærre og forklarer, at hans herre er blevet forhekset af troldmænd.

47.modern-en: Sancho walks beside the cage and argues with the curate that this is no enchantment he recognises from any romance.
47.modern-da: Sancho går ved siden af buret og diskuterer med præsten, at dette ikke er nogen forheksning, han kender fra nogen ridderroman.

48.modern-en: Sancho insists his master cannot be enchanted because he still eats, drinks, sleeps, and answers the call of nature like any other man.
48.modern-da: Sancho fastholder, at hans herre ikke kan være forhekset, eftersom han stadig spiser, drikker, sover og forretter sin nødtørft som ethvert andet menneske.

49.modern-en: Sancho urges Don Quixote out of the cage for a moment of dignity at the wayside and listens as the canon debates chivalric romances with him.
49.modern-da: Sancho overtaler Don Quixote til at komme ud af buret et øjeblik for værdighedens skyld ved vejkanten og lytter, mens domherren diskuterer ridderromaner med ham.

50.modern-en: Sancho counters the canon's scepticism with stories of his own, in particular his certainty that knight-errantry is real and his island awaits.
50.modern-da: Sancho imødegår domherrens skepsis med sine egne historier, især sin vished om, at den vandrende ridderstand er virkelig, og at hans ø venter.

52.modern-en: Sancho finally brings his master home in the cage at the end of the first sally, holding to the dream of governorship despite a beaten head and an empty purse.
52.modern-da: Sancho bringer endelig sin herre hjem i buret ved afslutningen af det første togt, mens han holder fast i drømmen om at blive guvernør trods en forslået skalle og en tom pung.

54.modern-en: Sancho fends off questions from the curate and barber, refusing to admit how restless he is to set out with his master again.
54.modern-da: Sancho afværger spørgsmål fra præsten og barberen og nægter at indrømme, hvor utålmodig han er efter at drage af sted med sin herre igen.

55.modern-en: Sancho is recruited for the third sally and persuades his wife Teresa that an island governor's wife is worth the worry of his absence.
55.modern-da: Sancho bliver hvervet til det tredje togt og overtaler sin kone Teresa til, at en øguvernørs kone er værd at bære savnet af hans fravær.

56.modern-en: Sancho rides out a third time with Don Quixote, the bachelor Sansón Carrasco having quietly approved the plan.
56.modern-da: Sancho rider ud for tredje gang med Don Quixote, efter at bachelaren Sansón Carrasco i al stilhed har godkendt planen.

57.modern-en: Sancho talks proverbs and country wisdom as the pair head toward El Toboso to ask Dulcinea's blessing.
57.modern-da: Sancho fremsiger ordsprog og bondevisdom, mens de to drager mod El Toboso for at bede om Dulcineas velsignelse.

58.modern-en: Sancho rides on in conversation with his master through the countryside.
58.modern-da: Sancho rider videre i samtale med sin herre gennem landskabet.

59.modern-en: Sancho leads the way into El Toboso by night, never having actually been there, and lets the donkeys pick the streets.
59.modern-da: Sancho fører an ind i El Toboso om natten, selv om han aldrig har været der, og lader æslerne vælge gaderne.

60.modern-en: Sancho is sent to fetch the lady Dulcinea from a village he has never set foot in, then sits down outside town to invent a way out.
60.modern-da: Sancho bliver sendt af sted for at hente fruen Dulcinea fra en landsby, han aldrig har sat sine ben i, og sætter sig så uden for byen for at finde på en udvej.

61.modern-en: Sancho hails three peasant girls on donkeys and presents them to Don Quixote as Dulcinea and her attendants come to meet him.
61.modern-da: Sancho råber til tre bondepiger på æsler og fremstiller dem for Don Quixote som Dulcinea og hendes ledsagere, der kommer ham i møde.

62.modern-en: Sancho swears that the coarse, garlic-smelling girl is the radiant Dulcinea, and convinces his master that wicked enchanters have transformed her.
62.modern-da: Sancho sværger på, at den grove, hvidløgslugtende pige er den strålende Dulcinea, og overbeviser sin herre om, at onde troldmænd har forvandlet hende.

63.modern-en: Sancho watches the cart of Death pass and helps his master back into the saddle when Rocinante shies.
63.modern-da: Sancho ser dødens kærre passere og hjælper sin herre op i sadlen igen, da Rocinante bliver sky.

64.modern-en: Sancho meets the Knight of the Mirrors' squire and trades fictions of squirely hardship and ambition with him through the night.
64.modern-da: Sancho møder Spejlridderens væbner og udveksler opdigtede historier om væbnerlivets strabadser og ærgerrighed med ham natten igennem.

65.modern-en: Sancho watches in disbelief as Don Quixote unhorses the Knight of the Mirrors, who, unmasked, has the face of his neighbour Sansón Carrasco.
65.modern-da: Sancho ser vantro til, mens Don Quixote kaster Spejlridderen af hesten, og ridderen, da han afsløres, har ansigtet af hans nabo Sansón Carrasco.

66.modern-en: Sancho rides on, refusing to believe what his eyes told him about Sansón's face on the defeated knight.
66.modern-da: Sancho rider videre og nægter at tro det, hans egne øjne fortalte ham om Sansóns ansigt på den besejrede ridder.

68.modern-en: Sancho dines with the green-coated gentleman and his family at Don Diego de Miranda's house.
68.modern-da: Sancho spiser hos den grønklædte herre og hans familie på Don Diego de Mirandas gård.

69.modern-en: Sancho is terrified when the carter announces caged lions and begs his master not to fight them.
69.modern-da: Sancho bliver skrækslagen, da kuskens bebuder bure med løver, og bønfalder sin herre om ikke at kæmpe mod dem.

70.modern-en: Sancho watches Don Quixote face down the open lion-cage, then provides the trembling carter with the tip Don Quixote leaves.
70.modern-da: Sancho ser Don Quixote trodse det åbne løvebur og giver derefter den skælvende kusk de drikkepenge, Don Quixote efterlader.

71.modern-en: Sancho enjoys the hospitality of Don Diego's house, eating better than he has in weeks.
71.modern-da: Sancho nyder gæstfriheden i Don Diegos hus og spiser bedre, end han har gjort i ugevis.

72.modern-en: Sancho rides with his master toward Camacho's wedding, talking of love and money as they go.
72.modern-da: Sancho rider med sin herre mod Camachos bryllup, mens de undervejs taler om kærlighed og penge.

73.modern-en: Sancho marvels at the lavish preparations for Camacho's feast and worries that he will not be allowed to eat his fill.
73.modern-da: Sancho undrer sig over de overdådige forberedelser til Camachos fest og bekymrer sig om, at han ikke får lov at spise sig mæt.

74.modern-en: Sancho lets Don Quixote down into the cave of Montesinos by rope and pulls him back up an hour later wrapped in his vision.
74.modern-da: Sancho firer Don Quixote ned i Montesinos' hule med et reb og hejser ham op igen en time senere, indhyllet i sit syn.

75.modern-en: Sancho listens to Don Quixote describe Dulcinea jumping like a goat and sending a maid to ask for a loan of six reals, and does not say whether he believes any of it.
75.modern-da: Sancho lytter til Don Quixote beskrive Dulcinea, der springer som en ged og sender en tjenestepige for at bede om et lån på seks reales, og siger ikke, om han tror på noget af det.

76.modern-en: Sancho rides on with his master past the meadow where the man with the lance and bagpipes pleads with them to come to the braying-village's battle.
76.modern-da: Sancho rider videre med sin herre forbi engen, hvor manden med lansen og sækkepiben bønfalder dem om at komme til skrydelandsbyens slag.

77.modern-en: Sancho is taken to Master Pedro's puppet show at the inn, where Don Quixote will shortly slash the puppets to pieces.
77.modern-da: Sancho bliver ført til mester Pedros dukketeater på kroen, hvor Don Quixote snart vil hugge dukkerne i stykker.

78.modern-en: Sancho stands by as Don Quixote demolishes the puppet stage, then helps settle the bill for the smashed figures.
78.modern-da: Sancho står ved siden af, mens Don Quixote raserer dukkescenen, og hjælper derefter med at gøre regningen for de knuste figurer op.

79.modern-en: Sancho is reluctantly dragged into the enchanted boat on the Ebro and laments the loss of his donkey when the boat overturns.
79.modern-da: Sancho bliver modvilligt slæbt om bord på den forheksede båd på Ebro og jamrer over tabet af sit æsel, da båden kæntrer.

80.modern-en: Sancho is fished out of the river with his master, soaked and complaining.
80.modern-da: Sancho bliver fisket op af floden sammen med sin herre, gennemblødt og brokkende.

81.modern-en: Sancho meets the duchess in the hunting party and is at once charmed by her interest in him.
81.modern-da: Sancho møder hertuginden i jagtselskabet og bliver straks bjergtaget af hendes interesse for ham.

82.modern-en: Sancho is seated with the lords at the ducal table, where his proverbs and appetite become the night's entertainment.
82.modern-da: Sancho får plads blandt de fornemme ved hertugbordet, hvor hans ordsprog og appetit bliver aftenens underholdning.

83.modern-en: Sancho talks at length with the duchess about his master, his wife, and his hopes for an island, oblivious to how thoroughly he is being studied.
83.modern-da: Sancho taler længe med hertuginden om sin herre, sin kone og sine håb om en ø, uvidende om hvor grundigt han bliver studeret.

84.modern-en: Sancho is grieved to learn that disenchanting Dulcinea will require three thousand and three hundred lashes on his own bare backside.
84.modern-da: Sancho bliver bedrøvet over at få at vide, at det vil kræve tre tusind tre hundrede piskeslag på hans egen bare bagdel at hæve forheksningen af Dulcinea.

85.modern-en: Sancho hears the Countess Trifaldi (the bearded duenna) recount her tale and is unsettled when he is told that he must ride on the wooden horse Clavileño with his master.
85.modern-da: Sancho hører grevinde Trifaldi (den skæggede hofdame) fortælle sin historie og bliver foruroliget, da han får at vide, at han skal ride på trææsten Clavileño sammen med sin herre.

86.modern-en: Sancho receives the duke's letter promising him the governorship of the island of Barataria.
86.modern-da: Sancho modtager hertugens brev, der lover ham guvernørposten over øen Barataria.

87.modern-en: Sancho is reminded again of the lashes owed for Dulcinea's disenchantment, and tries to bargain down the count.
87.modern-da: Sancho bliver atter mindet om de piskeslag, han skylder for Dulcineas befrielse, og forsøger at prutte tallet ned.

88.modern-en: Sancho is fitted out with bandages for his eyes ahead of the flight on Clavileño.
88.modern-da: Sancho bliver udstyret med bind for øjnene forud for flugten på Clavileño.

89.modern-en: Sancho prepares for the mock flight, embracing his master and asking him to remember Barataria.
89.modern-da: Sancho forbereder sig på den foregivne flyvetur, omfavner sin herre og beder ham huske Barataria.

90.modern-en: Sancho rides blindfolded on the wooden horse Clavileño with Don Quixote, swears afterwards to have seen the stars and patted she-goats among the constellations.
90.modern-da: Sancho rider med bind for øjnene på trææsten Clavileño sammen med Don Quixote og sværger bagefter på at have set stjernerne og klappet hunkønsgeder blandt stjernebillederne.

91.modern-en: Sancho is congratulated on his "voyage" by the duke and duchess and asked to describe what he saw above the clouds.
91.modern-da: Sancho bliver lykønsket med sin »rejse« af hertugen og hertuginden og bedt om at beskrive, hvad han så over skyerne.

92.modern-en: Sancho is briefed on the wooden horse's destruction and reminded that his governorship awaits.
92.modern-da: Sancho bliver orienteret om trææstens ødelæggelse og mindet om, at hans guvernørpost venter.

93.modern-en: Sancho receives a long stream of advice from Don Quixote on how to rule his island justly before setting out.
93.modern-da: Sancho modtager en lang strøm af råd fra Don Quixote om, hvordan han skal styre sin ø retfærdigt, inden han drager af sted.

94.modern-en: Sancho is given further private counsel by his master on table manners, dress, and speech for the governorship.
94.modern-da: Sancho får yderligere fortrolige formaninger af sin herre om bordskik, klædedragt og tale med henblik på guvernørposten.

95.modern-en: Sancho prepares to depart for Barataria and writes (via a secretary) a letter to his wife Teresa about his coming greatness.
95.modern-da: Sancho forbereder sin afrejse til Barataria og skriver (gennem en sekretær) et brev til sin kone Teresa om sin forestående storhed.

96.modern-en: Sancho is escorted in state to Barataria to take up the governorship, while Don Quixote is left at the castle to be ambushed by a wave of cats.
96.modern-da: Sancho bliver højtideligt eskorteret til Barataria for at tiltræde guvernørposten, mens Don Quixote bliver efterladt på slottet for at blive overfaldet af en sværm af katte.

97.modern-en: Sancho takes his seat as governor of Barataria and judges his first cases with surprising shrewdness.
97.modern-da: Sancho indtager sin plads som guvernør af Barataria og dømmer sine første sager med overraskende skarpsindighed.

99.modern-en: Sancho continues governing Barataria, sitting in judgment, dispensing proverbs, and beginning to feel hungry as his physician forbids every dish.
99.modern-da: Sancho fortsætter med at styre Barataria, sidder til doms, øser af sine ordsprog og begynder at blive sulten, efterhånden som hans læge forbyder ham hver eneste ret.

101.modern-en: Sancho makes his nightly rounds as governor and listens to the city's small dramas, including the runaway daughter dressed as a boy.
101.modern-da: Sancho går sin natlige runde som guvernør og lytter til byens små dramaer, deriblandt den bortløbne datter klædt ud som dreng.

103.modern-en: Sancho receives a letter from his master and writes one back, governing soberly but already worn down by office.
103.modern-da: Sancho modtager et brev fra sin herre og skriver et tilbage, idet han regerer besindigt, men allerede er slidt af embedet.

104.modern-en: Sancho's wife Teresa receives news from court of her husband's governorship and replies in proud, bewildered village language.
104.modern-da: Sanchos kone Teresa modtager nyt fra hoffet om sin mands guvernørpost og svarer i stolt, forvirret landsbysprog.

105.modern-en: Sancho endures a staged night attack on Barataria, is trussed between two shields and trampled, and decides at dawn to resign the governorship and rejoin his master.
105.modern-da: Sancho udholder et iscenesat natligt angreb på Barataria, bliver snøret ind mellem to skjolde og trampet ned og beslutter ved daggry at nedlægge guvernørposten og slutte sig til sin herre igen.

106.modern-en: Sancho rides back toward the ducal castle and falls into a pit where, in the dark, he laments his governorship as soberly as anything he has yet said.
106.modern-da: Sancho rider tilbage mod hertugslottet og falder ned i et hul, hvor han i mørket beklager sin guvernørtid så besindigt som noget, han endnu har sagt.

107.modern-en: Sancho is hauled out of the pit and welcomed back by Don Quixote, who is glad to have his squire restored.
107.modern-da: Sancho bliver halet op af hullet og budt velkommen tilbage af Don Quixote, som er glad for at have sin væbner igen.

108.modern-en: Sancho is back at his master's side as the company leaves the castle and rides on.
108.modern-da: Sancho er tilbage ved sin herres side, mens følget forlader slottet og rider videre.

109.modern-en: Sancho keeps Don Quixote company on the road and listens to him plan the pastoral life if knight-errantry is denied him.
109.modern-da: Sancho holder Don Quixote med selskab på vejen og lytter til ham lægge planer om hyrdelivet, hvis den vandrende ridderstand nægtes ham.

110.modern-en: Sancho is trampled along with his master when a herd of bulls is driven over them.
110.modern-da: Sancho bliver trampet ned sammen med sin herre, da en flok tyre drives hen over dem.

111.modern-en: Sancho recovers at a wayside inn and hears travellers debate the second, spurious Don Quixote published by Avellaneda.
111.modern-da: Sancho kommer sig på en vejkro og hører rejsende diskutere den anden, falske Don Quixote, som Avellaneda har udgivet.

112.modern-en: Sancho rides on with Don Quixote, who has changed course to avoid the false Don Quixote of the rival book.
112.modern-da: Sancho rider videre med Don Quixote, der har ændret rute for at undgå den falske Don Quixote fra den rivaliserende bog.

113.modern-en: Sancho continues alongside his master toward Barcelona.
113.modern-da: Sancho fortsætter ved sin herres side mod Barcelona.

114.modern-en: Sancho is hung up by the foot from a tree by the bandit Roque Guinart's men along with his master, then freed when Roque recognises Don Quixote.
114.modern-da: Sancho bliver hængt op i foden i et træ af røveren Roque Guinarts mænd sammen med sin herre og bliver derefter løsladt, da Roque genkender Don Quixote.

115.modern-en: Sancho rides with Roque Guinart's band toward Barcelona, fascinated by the bandit's command.
115.modern-da: Sancho rider med Roque Guinarts bande mod Barcelona, fascineret af røverens myndighed.

116.modern-en: Sancho watches his master overthrown on the beach of Barcelona by the Knight of the White Moon (Sansón Carrasco in disguise), the worst day of his squire's life.
116.modern-da: Sancho ser sin herre kastet af hesten på Barcelonas strand af Ridderen af den Hvide Måne (Sansón Carrasco i forklædning), den værste dag i hans væbnerliv.

117.modern-en: Sancho hears Don Quixote announce that, since knight-errantry is forbidden him for a year, they will become shepherds.
117.modern-da: Sancho hører Don Quixote forkynde, at de, eftersom den vandrende ridderstand er ham forbudt i et år, vil blive hyrder.

118.modern-en: Sancho rides homeward with Don Quixote, now and then asked to begin paying off the lashes that will disenchant Dulcinea.
118.modern-da: Sancho rider hjemad med Don Quixote og bliver nu og da bedt om at begynde at afbetale de piskeslag, der skal befri Dulcinea.

119.modern-en: Sancho fakes the night's lashes by beating the trees beside him while groaning loudly enough to satisfy his master.
119.modern-da: Sancho fingerer nattens piskeslag ved at slå på træerne ved siden af sig, mens han stønner højt nok til at stille sin herre tilfreds.

120.modern-en: Sancho continues the road home and the slow accounting of his self-flagellation debt for Dulcinea.
120.modern-da: Sancho fortsætter ad vejen hjem og det langsomme regnskab over sin selvpiskningsgæld for Dulcinea.

121.modern-en: Sancho refuses to be hurried into finishing the lashes and bargains his way through each instalment.
121.modern-da: Sancho nægter at lade sig jage til at gøre piskeslagene færdige og pruttede sig vej gennem hvert afdrag.

122.modern-en: Sancho is trampled by pigs along with Don Quixote on the road and takes it as one indignity too many.
122.modern-da: Sancho bliver trampet ned af svin sammen med Don Quixote på vejen og tager det som en ydmygelse for meget.

123.modern-en: Sancho returns to his village with Don Quixote at last, his pouch fuller than his ambitions.
123.modern-da: Sancho vender omsider tilbage til sin landsby med Don Quixote, med pungen federe end hans ambitioner.

124.modern-en: Sancho greets his wife Teresa and daughter Sanchica at home, telling them of governorship and disenchantments at once.
124.modern-da: Sancho hilser sin kone Teresa og datteren Sanchica derhjemme og fortæller dem om guvernørpost og forheksninger på én gang.

125.modern-en: Sancho sits at his master's bedside as Don Quixote sickens, urging him to get up and live as a shepherd, weeping when he sees how serious the illness is.
125.modern-da: Sancho sidder ved sin herres seng, mens Don Quixote bliver syg, opfordrer ham til at stå op og leve som hyrde og græder, da han ser, hvor alvorlig sygdommen er.

126.modern-en: Sancho weeps at the bedside as Don Quixote dies, having heard his master renounce chivalry, and is named in the will with his wages and a remembrance.
126.modern-da: Sancho græder ved sengen, mens Don Quixote dør, efter at have hørt sin herre give afkald på ridderlivet, og bliver nævnt i testamentet med sin løn og en erindringsgave.

epithet.en: The peasant girl Don Quixote has elevated into his unseen lady
epithet.da: Bondepigen, Don Quixote har ophøjet til sin uskuede dame

1.modern-en: Dulcinea del Toboso is invented as the lady of Don Quixote's thoughts; the real Aldonza Lorenzo, a farm girl from El Toboso, is rechristened to suit a knight-errant's vow.
1.modern-da: Dulcinea del Toboso opfindes som damen i Don Quixotes tanker; den virkelige Aldonza Lorenzo, en bondepige fra El Toboso, omdøbes for at passe til en vandrende ridders løfte.

2.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked from the saddle as Don Quixote rides out, begging his lady to remember her wretched vassal as he goes to do her honour.
2.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes fra saddelen, da Don Quixote rider ud, og han bønfalder sin dame om at huske sin ynkelige vasal, mens han drager af sted for at ære hende.

3.modern-en: Dulcinea is named in Don Quixote's vigil and his vows during the mock-dubbing at the inn.
3.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes under Don Quixotes nattevagt og hans løfter ved den narrede ridderslagning på kroen.

4.modern-en: Dulcinea is the cause Don Quixote demands the merchants of Toledo swear to without ever having seen her, and the reason he charges them when they refuse.
4.modern-da: Dulcinea er den sag, Don Quixote kræver, at købmændene fra Toledo skal sværge på uden nogensinde at have set hende, og grunden til, at han angriber dem, da de nægter.

5.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked in Don Quixote's delirium after his fall, the labourer carrying home a man muttering his lady's name.
5.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes i Don Quixotes vildelse efter hans fald, idet bonden bærer en mand hjem, der mumler sin dames navn.

8.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked as Don Quixote charges the windmills, calling on her to defend her knight in his hour of need.
8.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes, da Don Quixote angriber vejrmøllerne og beder hende forsvare sin ridder i hans nødens stund.

9.modern-en: Dulcinea is named in the rediscovered Arabic manuscript through Cide Hamete Benengeli's mocking marginal note that she had the best hand in La Mancha for salting pigs.
9.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes i det genfundne arabiske håndskrift gennem Cide Hamete Benengelis hånlige randbemærkning om, at hun havde den bedste hånd i hele La Mancha til at salte svinekød.

10.modern-en: Dulcinea is named in Don Quixote's account of why his enemies must be sent in homage to El Toboso.
10.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes i Don Quixotes forklaring på, hvorfor hans fjender skal sendes som hyldest til El Toboso.

12.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked in conversation with the goatherds as the lady whose service governs every action of her knight.
12.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes i samtalen med gedehyrderne som den dame, hvis tjeneste styrer hver eneste af hendes ridders handlinger.

13.modern-en: Dulcinea is praised by Don Quixote to the gentlemen riding to Chrysostom's burial as without peer among all the ladies of literature.
13.modern-da: Dulcinea prises af Don Quixote over for herrerne, der rider til Chrysostoms begravelse, som uden lige blandt alle litteraturens damer.

16.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked in Don Quixote's apology to Maritornes in the dark, his bruised heart still bound to a lady he has never seen.
16.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes i Don Quixotes undskyldning til Maritornes i mørket, idet hans forslåede hjerte stadig er bundet til en dame, han aldrig har set.

17.modern-en: Dulcinea is the unseen lady whose memory steadies Don Quixote through the night of the holy balm.
17.modern-da: Dulcinea er den usete dame, hvis minde holder Don Quixote rolig gennem natten med den hellige balsam.

20.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked through the long night of fulling-mill terror as Don Quixote commits his fate to her.
20.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes gennem den lange nat med rædsel ved stampemøllen, idet Don Quixote overgiver sin skæbne til hende.

22.modern-en: Dulcinea is named when Don Quixote orders the freed galley slaves to present themselves to her in El Toboso, a command they reward with a hail of stones.
22.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes, da Don Quixote befaler de befriede galejslaver at melde sig hos hende i El Toboso, en befaling de belønner med en byge af sten.

23.modern-en: Dulcinea is named in Don Quixote's resolution to imitate Amadis in the Sierra Morena for love of her.
23.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes i Don Quixotes beslutning om at efterligne Amadis i Sierra Morena af kærlighed til hende.

25.modern-en: Dulcinea is named again and again as Don Quixote strips for his penance in the Sierra and composes a letter for Sancho to carry to her at El Toboso.
25.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes gang på gang, idet Don Quixote klæder sig af til sin bod i Sierra og forfatter et brev, som Sancho skal bringe hende i El Toboso.

26.modern-en: Dulcinea is the object of an extended Sierra-Morena soliloquy of love, poetry, and sighs as Don Quixote continues his self-imposed penance.
26.modern-da: Dulcinea er genstand for en langtrukken eneudtale i Sierra Morena fuld af kærlighed, poesi og suk, mens Don Quixote fortsætter sin selvpålagte bod.

27.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked as Don Quixote sings of his suffering to whoever might overhear.
27.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes, idet Don Quixote synger om sin lidelse for enhver, der måtte overhøre ham.

29.modern-en: Dulcinea is named in Don Quixote's first protests when "Princess Micomicona" appears, since marrying her would mean betraying his lady.
29.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes i Don Quixotes første protester, da »Prinsesse Micomicona« dukker op, eftersom et ægteskab med hende ville betyde forræderi mod hans dame.

30.modern-en: Dulcinea is firmly upheld as the only lady Don Quixote will serve, even as Dorotea (as Micomicona) presses her suit.
30.modern-da: Dulcinea fastholdes bestemt som den eneste dame, Don Quixote vil tjene, selv da Dorotea (som Micomicona) trænger sig på med sit frieri.

31.modern-en: Dulcinea is described to Don Quixote by Sancho's improvised account: winnowing wheat, robust, country-handsome, and pleased to send her greetings to her knight.
31.modern-da: Dulcinea beskrives for Don Quixote i Sanchos improviserede beretning: hun renser hvede, er robust, landlig-køn og glad for at sende sin ridder sine hilsener.

43.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked as Don Quixote, hanging by the wrist from the inn window, takes Maritornes's hand for hers in the dark.
43.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes, da Don Quixote, hængende ved håndleddet fra krovinduet, i mørket tager Maritornes' hånd for hendes.

46.modern-en: Dulcinea is named in Don Quixote's farewells as he is loaded into the enchanted cage to be brought home.
46.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes i Don Quixotes farvel, idet han læsses ind i det fortryllede bur for at blive bragt hjem.

48.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked as Don Quixote argues for the reality of the knight-errantry that keeps him in the cage.
48.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes, idet Don Quixote argumenterer for virkeligheden af det vandrende ridderskab, der holder ham i buret.

52.modern-en: Dulcinea is named one last time before the first sally ends, as Don Quixote charges the procession of penitents in defence of a captive lady.
52.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes en sidste gang, før det første togt ender, idet Don Quixote angriber processionen af bodsgængere til forsvar for en fanget dame.

54.modern-en: Dulcinea is on Don Quixote's lips at home, the year of recovery doing nothing to dim her place in his mind.
54.modern-da: Dulcinea er på Don Quixotes læber derhjemme, og hele rekonvalescensåret formår ikke at svække hendes plads i hans sind.

55.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked as Don Quixote and Sancho plan the third sally, with a planned visit to El Toboso to receive her blessing.
55.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes, da Don Quixote og Sancho planlægger det tredje togt med et planlagt besøg i El Toboso for at modtage hendes velsignelse.

56.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked as the destination of the third sally is set: a road that leads to El Toboso.
56.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes, idet målet for det tredje togt fastlægges: en vej, der fører til El Toboso.

60.modern-en: Dulcinea is to be sought out in El Toboso, but Sancho cannot point her house out in the dark and Don Quixote rides off to hide in the wood.
60.modern-da: Dulcinea skal opsøges i El Toboso, men Sancho kan ikke udpege hendes hus i mørket, og Don Quixote rider af sted for at gemme sig i skoven.

61.modern-en: Dulcinea is conjured by Sancho out of three peasant girls riding donkeys, with the squire bowing low before the lady he has invented.
61.modern-da: Dulcinea fremmanes af Sancho ud af tre bondepiger, der rider på æsler, idet væbneren bukker dybt for den dame, han har opfundet.

62.modern-en: Dulcinea is, in Sancho's solemn invention, present in person as the garlicky farm girl now declared enchanted by sages who have hidden her true beauty.
62.modern-da: Dulcinea er, i Sanchos højtidelige opfindelse, til stede i egen person som den hvidløgsdunstende bondepige, der nu erklæres fortryllet af troldmænd, som har skjult hendes sande skønhed.

63.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked as Don Quixote tries to recover from the shock of seeing her in such a coarse form.
63.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes, idet Don Quixote forsøger at komme sig over chokket ved at se hende i så grov en skikkelse.

66.modern-en: Dulcinea is sworn to by Don Quixote as he forces the defeated Knight of the Mirrors to admit her supremacy among ladies.
66.modern-da: Dulcinea sværges der ved af Don Quixote, idet han tvinger den besejrede Spejlridder til at indrømme hendes overlegenhed blandt damer.

68.modern-en: Dulcinea is praised to Don Diego de Miranda's family as the noblest lady alive, though enchanted into peasant form.
68.modern-da: Dulcinea prises over for Don Diego de Mirandas familie som den ædleste dame, der lever, om end fortryllet til bondeskikkelse.

69.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked as Don Quixote prepares to face the lions in her name.
69.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes, idet Don Quixote forbereder sig på at møde løverne i hendes navn.

70.modern-en: Dulcinea is named as the lady on whose behalf the lion-feat is performed, the Knight of the Lions earning a new title in her honour.
70.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes som den dame, til hvis ære løvebedriften udføres, idet Løveridderen erhverver en ny titel til hendes ære.

72.modern-en: Dulcinea is mentioned in Don Quixote's discourse on love and worth as he rides on.
72.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes i Don Quixotes tale om kærlighed og værd, mens han rider videre.

73.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked when love-talk turns serious at Camacho's wedding.
73.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes, da snakken om kærlighed bliver alvorlig ved Camachos bryllup.

74.modern-en: Dulcinea is to be sought even in the depths of the cave of Montesinos, Don Quixote tying the rope around himself in her name.
74.modern-da: Dulcinea skal opsøges selv i dybet af Montesinos' hule, idet Don Quixote binder rebet om sig i hendes navn.

75.modern-en: Dulcinea is glimpsed below ground in Don Quixote's vision: still enchanted in peasant form, jumping like a goat, and dispatching a maid to ask her knight for the loan of six reals on a petticoat.
75.modern-da: Dulcinea ses under jorden i Don Quixotes syn: stadig fortryllet i bondeskikkelse, springende som en ged, og hun sender en tjenestepige af sted for at bede sin ridder om at låne hende seks reales mod pant i et underskørt.

76.modern-en: Dulcinea is the haunting subject of Don Quixote's conversation after emerging from the cave, his vision of her grief shaping every thought.
76.modern-da: Dulcinea er det hjemsøgende emne for Don Quixotes samtale, efter han er kommet op af hulen, idet hans syn af hendes sorg præger hver eneste tanke.

81.modern-en: Dulcinea is invoked at the duke and duchess's hunting party as the lady whose disenchantment is the knight's great unfinished business.
81.modern-da: Dulcinea påkaldes ved hertugens og hertugindens jagtselskab som den dame, hvis affortryllelse er ridderens store uafsluttede opgave.

82.modern-en: Dulcinea is woven into the ducal entertainments as the enchantments around the household begin.
82.modern-da: Dulcinea væves ind i de hertugelige forlystelser, idet fortryllelserne omkring husstanden tager deres begyndelse.

84.modern-en: Dulcinea is the lady whose disenchantment Merlin (or his impersonator at the duke's pageant) declares can only be brought about by three thousand three hundred lashes on Sancho's bare backside.
84.modern-da: Dulcinea er den dame, hvis affortryllelse Merlin (eller den, der udgiver sig for ham ved hertugens optog) erklærer kun kan opnås ved tre tusind tre hundrede piskeslag på Sanchos bare bagdel.

85.modern-en: Dulcinea's disenchantment is pressed on Sancho again as the bearded Countess Trifaldi joins the duke's masque.
85.modern-da: Dulcineas affortryllelse trænges atter ind på Sancho, idet den skæggede grevinde Trifaldi slutter sig til hertugens maskespil.

86.modern-en: Dulcinea is named as the prize behind the wooden-horse adventure that the duke and duchess are arranging.
86.modern-da: Dulcinea nævnes som præmien bag eventyret med trææsten, som hertugen og hertuginden er ved at arrangere.

87.modern-en: Dulcinea's disenchantment is restated with elaborate solemnity: only Sancho's self-administered lashes will free her from the peasant-form into which the sages have cast her.
